quote: The concept of implementation fidelity is currently described and defined in the literature in terms of five elements that need to be measured [ 1 , 2 , 4 ]. implementation fidelity
quote: Despite being viewed as an element of implementation fidelity by the literature, programme differentiation actually measures something distinct from fidelity. It is concerned with determining those elements that are essential for its success. This exercise is an important part of any evaluation of new interventions. It enables discovery of those elements that make a difference to outcomes and whether some elements are redundant. Such so-called "essential" elements may be discovered either by canvassing the designers of the intervention or, preferably, by "component analysis", assessing the effect of the intervention on outcomes and determining which components have the most impact [ 17 ]. This element would therefore be more usefully described as the "Identification of an intervention's essential components".

quote: The measurement of implementation fidelity is the measurement of adherence, i.e ., how far those responsible for delivering an intervention actually adhere to the intervention as it is outlined by its designers. The level achieved may be influenced or affected, ( i.e ., moderated) by certain other variables: intervention complexity, facilitation strategies, quality of delivery, and participant responsiveness.

value: Specificity
quote: Detailed or specific interventions have been found to be more likely to be implemented with high fidelity than ones that are vague.
